title: Identifiability of electromagnetic and chemical contributions to SERS
research_question: Under which independently testable assumptions and measurements can electromagnetic field enhancement and molecule-surface chemical enhancement be separated for mode-resolved SERS when geometry, orientation, charge-transfer states and optical response may be coupled? Can an unexplored physical dependency or experimental contrast overcome an identifiable limitation of existing methods?
success_definition: Propose a physically viable mechanistic or identifiability advance, derive a nontrivial quantitative prediction that a strong established null cannot reproduce under stated controls, and specify independent falsification. It is acceptable to abstain; novelty and correctness require independent assessment.
epistemic_scope: This is an open research problem definition, NOT a claim that no existing separation method exists. Reported reference statements below are summaries of abstract/review statements and must not be treated as complete full-text audits.
known_physics: A working intensity factorization for a mode k may involve molecular number, incident and emitted near-field factors, orientation-dependent Raman tensor and molecule-surface electronic interactions. Its independent-factor interpretation is an approximation, not a universal theorem.
A single scalar Raman intensity does not uniquely identify two independent latent multiplicative enhancement factors without calibrated constraints or additional observables.

Chemical and electromagnetic enhancement are not always operationally independent: adsorbates change dielectric response and local fields, and the local field interacts with molecular orientation and chemical polarizability.
DFT/TDDFT-based schemes that isolate a calculated EM contribution from chemical enhancement have already been published. Merely repeating this separation is not a novelty claim.
open_gaps: In a specified molecular and plasmonic geometry, what *observable combinations* make the decomposition structurally identifiable rather than underdetermined?
Which independent perturbation removes the ambiguity between orientation/coverage change and interfacial electronic-state change?
When would an interaction/cross term invalidate a naive product EM × CHEM decomposition?
Can a proposed mechanism predict an observable scaling, sign, threshold or regime boundary not obtained from an explicit best conventional countermodel?
measurement_limits: No new experimental measurements, calibrations or molecule-specific first-principles simulations are present in this packet.
References do not imply that their experimental systems, analyte identities, geometries or quantitative conclusions transfer to all SERS substrates.
Any proposed parameter magnitude, gradient, dimensionless number, or new state variable must be checked against feasible physical bounds before advancing a discovery claim.

references.title: A Unified View of Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
references.supported_summary: Describes plasmon-resonance, metal-molecule charge-transfer and molecular resonances as distinct contributing mechanisms; it does not establish a universally unique empirical decomposition.

references.title: On the relative magnitudes of the electromagnetic and chemical enhancements to the SERS effect
references.supported_summary: Reports an experimental comparison using external reflection and attenuated total reflection for an electrochemically activated Ag/KCl/pyridine system; applicability is system-specific.

references.title: Theoretical Procedure for Precise Evaluation of Chemical Enhancement in Molecular Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
references.supported_summary: Presents an atomistic DFT/TDDFT procedure to separate EM and chemical contributions in BPDT sandwiched between small Au clusters; this is established prior art for decomposition methods, not a generic validation for every real substrate.

references.title: Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy: Current Understanding, Challenges, and Opportunities
references.supported_summary: Surveys electromagnetic enhancement, charge-transfer-related mechanisms and the importance of spectrum-structure correlation. No claim of an unsolved unique decomposition in all regimes is made here.

references.title: A Review on Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
references.supported_summary: Reviews near-field incident/emitted wavelength factors, molecular chemical changes and orientation dependence; notes the EM/CHEM separation is not always clear-cut.
